A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework and retain matching methods, datasets and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original training-time and decoding experiments on MATH, UltraFeedback and Socratic Mind, together with head-weight, discount-factor and decoding-continuity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds baseline comparisons, conflict and robustness experiments, computational measurements, and independent model and human evaluations.

M1.justification: The formal ensemble rule changes from averaging head probabilities in v1 Equation 5 to applying softmax to weighted logits in v2 Equation 4. Since v1 already described logit ensembling in prose, this corrects an inconsistent specification without establishing an implementation change. The architecture, DPO objectives, PRM training and cache-based decoding remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: The three domains and their objective types are retained. v2 adds a deliberately selected population of 7,500 Human Values preference pairs with opposing helpfulness and honesty preferences (Appendix E.2), extending coverage to an explicit conflict scenario. The five-head experiment reuses existing math and human-values tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds DPO Soup to the Math and Human Values training comparisons in Table 1, and evaluates scalarized Multi-Objective PPO in Human Values in Table 19. These introduce parameter-merging and PPO comparator families beyond v1's SFT and DPO-based comparisons. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Original domain training settings and default decoding budgets are retained. New protocols include five-head joint training on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, alternative segmentation rules, probabilistic overrides of PRM selection, controlled latency/memory measurements, GPT-4o evaluation on 500 math problems, and three-annotator evaluation on 100 problems. These substantially expand the evaluation design rather than establish reruns of the original experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds segmentation sensitivity and PRM-selection-noise studies, explicit objective-conflict tests, five-objective scaling, qualitative interaction examples, computational overhead comparisons, and cross-model/human validation (Section 6.4 and Appendices C, E and F). The original discount-factor, head-weight and hidden-state-versus-text analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averages and standard deviations; additional result rows do not establish increased replication. v2 adds human-majority/judge agreement analysis, including 77.0% agreement and Cohen's kappa of 0.45 in Appendix F.2. This introduces an agreement statistic without adding confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained numerical entries in all eleven original tables are unchanged. v2 adds substantial results: MOPPO scores 0.6764/0.2921/0.1460 on helpfulness/honesty/truthfulness (Table 19), cached PRM-guided decoding achieves a reported 4.2-fold speedup (Table 6), and human-majority engagement ratings are 64% for Base versus 87% for MAH-DPO (Table 22). Conflict, scaling, segmentation and noise results are also new.

T1.justification: The ensemble distribution is mathematically revised from a probability mixture to softmax of a logit mixture, which is not an equivalent expression. Otherwise, the PRM targets and DPO mathematics are retained. Gradient and computational analyses move to Appendices B.1 and C.1 without new proofs or substantive derivation changes.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain standardized PRM training across reward types, vectorized MAH-DPO, and controllable inference-time alignment. MAHALO names the existing framework. Cross-domain PRM transfer and reward-verifiability takeaways foregrounded in v2's introduction were already present in v1's findings; the new experiments strengthen support without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially qualifies the interpretation of objective compatibility: average correlations conceal conflicting examples, and the Human Values ensemble no longer dominates both specialists under explicit conflict. It adds explanations contrasting head-level gradient isolation with shared-representation updates, interprets sensitivity to PRM quality, and acknowledges limits concerning scaling beyond five objectives and moderate human–judge agreement.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies that the frozen reference policy shares no parameters with the trainable policy and discloses equal objective weights and balanced sampling. It also supplies hardware and settings for the new computational benchmarks and construction details for added studies. Existing domain hyperparameters, system prompts and the code-access URL are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds a focused discussion of interference and data/gradient compatibility, citing Dong's SFT-composition work, Wu's Mixture-of-Skills, and Liang's 2025/2026 work. Safe RLHF is newly cited for the PPO comparison, while some background references are removed. The overall PRM and multi-objective positioning remains stable; numerous publication-metadata updates do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the introduction around practical takeaways, condenses background and findings, and introduces the MAHALO terminology. It moves gradient analysis and decoding details into reorganized appendices, relocates the ethics material, adds an impact statement, and moves system prompts to the end. This changes the narrative organization beyond accommodating new experiments.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout. Existing figures and tables are resized and relocated, Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix C, and numerous tables display the new analyses. Appendix result tables are regrouped and prompt boxes reflow across different pages.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1's support for its central claims: it tests explicitly conflicting preferences, broadens comparator families, measures computational costs, and independently validates engagement gains with GPT-4o and humans. These additions substantially strengthen empirical credibility and clarify applicability limits. Human agreement remains moderate, and v2 gives inconsistent Socratic PRM backbone descriptions in A.3 and F.1, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
